# 2 Baruch Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**11:1** And-I-Baruch went-out and-sat-down under-an-oak that-was-on-the-bank-of-the-river-Kidron, and-no-one-knew-of-me.

**11:2** And-I-sat-there and-mourned over-Zion, and-I-wept-bitterly.

**11:3** And-I-cried-out and-lamented and-said: "Thou hast-not-spared-Zion, O-LORD! And-thou-hast-not-delivered-Jerusalem!"

**11:4** "Where-now is-the-multitude-of-thy-mercies? And-where-are-the-things-of-thy-grace, with-which-you-didst-deal-bountifully in-each-generation-after-generation?

**11:5** And-I-continued-weeping and-mourning-for-seven-days.

**11:6** And-after-seven-days the-word-of-the-LORD came-to-me.

**11:7** And-he-said-to-me: "Hast-thou-indeed-set-thy-heart on-all-these-things that-have-come-upon-Zion? Is-thy-heart-troubled, O-Baruch, over-what-has-befallen-Jerusalem?

---

*EMET notes: Baruch mourns at the Kidron Valley, the eastern boundary of Jerusalem. The seven-day mourning period (v.5) is a standard mourning convention (cf. Job 2:13). The divine word breaks the mourning at the end of the chapter.*
